USD.catalyst: The US Dollar Index trades near 98.84, remaining below its 20-day (99.30) and 200-day (99.13) moving averages as market participants parse incoming inflation data ahead of the Federal Reserve policy announcement. GBP.catalyst: Sterling trades around 1.3541 against the dollar, holding above its 50-day (1.3467) and 200-day (1.3450) moving averages as market participants digest hawkish policy signals from Bank of England officials. BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill and Governor Andrew Bailey have highlighted persistent worries regarding energy-driven inflation, reinforcing market expectations that the Monetary Policy Committee will proceed cautiously regarding rate cuts. A deepening split on the MPC is visible as external member Megan Greene urges vigilance against secondary price shocks, while Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden favors a more patient approach ahead of the September 17 policy decision. UK fiscal concerns ahead of Parliament's return continue to act as a secondary headwind, keeping sterling price action tightly anchored to upcoming inflation and business activity surveys.

EUR.catalyst: The euro holds steady near 1.1627 against the greenback, positioned above its 20-day (1.1619) and 50-day (1.1520) moving averages as traders prepare for the European Central Bank's rate decision. Markets broadly anticipate that ECB President Christine Lagarde and the Governing Council will keep key interest rates unchanged, maintaining the deposit facility rate at 2.00% following recent eurozone inflation and growth metrics that beat consensus expectations. Nomura notes that policy divergence between a paused ECB and an easing Federal Reserve could provide structural medium-term support for the single currency into 2026. However, disappointing eurozone retail sales figures continue to cap immediate upside, leaving swaps markets pricing limited probability of further rate hikes this year.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen has emerged as the strongest G10 performer over the past week, advancing 1.47% on a composite basis as short-covering accelerates ahead of the Bank of Japan's September 17–18 policy meeting. Short positions held by leveraged funds—which reached an extreme net short of -111,297 contracts on CFTC data—are unwinding rapidly as market pricing points to a potential 25-basis-point BOJ rate hike to 1.25%. Sentiment has been further bolstered by the Reuters Tankan index, which showed Japanese factory sentiment rising to a near five-year high on robust semiconductor demand, alongside ongoing verbal intervention warnings from Tokyo officials. The currency's sharp appreciation has driven spot rates well below key technical handles, pushing major pairs below their respective 20-day and 200-day moving average clusters.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar demonstrates steady performance near 1.3781 against the U.S. dollar, holding below its 20-day (1.3848) and 50-day (1.3988) moving average resistance lines. Upward risks to Canadian inflation flagged by the Bank of Canada have prompted investors to increase bets on monetary tightening in the coming months, providing structural support to the loonie. Additional support stems from U.S. labor market deceleration, which reinforces market expectations of Fed rate cuts and narrows the cross-border yield spread. Market participants are monitoring trade developments between the U.S. and Canada, though price action remains primarily governed by central bank policy expectations and energy market fluctuations.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar has underperformed its G10 peers over the past week, declining 1.05% on a composite basis and trading near 0.5856 against the U.S. dollar. Pressure on the kiwi follows monetary policy signals indicating the Reserve Bank of New Zealand may keep official cash rates lower for longer relative to global peers, narrowing New Zealand's yield advantage. RBNZ Governor Christian Hawkesby and committee members are weighing economic slack against future rate path projections, with markets watching whether the official cash rate shifts toward 3.25% by year-end. In capital markets, the International Finance Corporation completed a record NZD 1 billion Kauri bond transaction, though primary driver dynamics remain dominated by broader risk aversion and geopolitical developments.

NOK.catalyst: The Norwegian krone has posted modest weekly gains, rising 0.89% on a composite basis as underlying inflation pressures keep Norges Bank policymakers aligned with a hawkish stance. Economists and market participants continue to speculate whether the central bank's monetary policy committee will maintain elevated interest rates to cool domestic spending and bring inflation back to target. Settlement of Norwegian krone foreign exchange transactions continues seamlessly via CLS accounts at Norges Bank, supported by liquidity arrangements under the Scandinavian Cash Pool. Spot price action remains anchored above medium-term support levels, with technical positioning keeping the currency below its 20-day (9.345) and 200-day (9.618) moving average thresholds against the dollar.
